samples.summary: DocStore interface contract for `applyCellStyle` still documents the old "additive only" semantics that this delta invalidates
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:117-118 declares: "Apply partial cell style (background, borders, alignment) via styleByPath. Additive only — setting a property to undefined will not remove it from the tree." Both implementations now violate that: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2444-2462 removes any key present-with-`undefined` via `removeStyleByPath`, and packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:287 normalizes `''` to an explicit `undefined`. Any future implementer or caller reading this interface comment (it is the only place the cross-store contract is stated, alongside `applyCellSpan`'s comment at :123-125 which *does* describe removal) will code against a contract that no longer holds. Fix belongs on store.ts: document the `''`/`undefined` = "clear this key" convention.

samples.summary: Removal path keys on *any* explicitly-undefined cell-style key, silently widening the contract beyond the `''` background sentinel
samples.evidence: `removedCellStyleAttrs` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2251-2255) matches `key in style && style[key] === undefined` for all seven cell attrs, so a caller that spreads a partial object containing e.g. `{ padding: undefined, verticalAlign: undefined }` — previously a harmless no-op because `styleByPath` merged and `serializeCellStyle` skipped falsy values — now deletes those attributes from the CRDT. Reachable through `EditorAPI.applyTableCellStyle` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3413-3436), which passes the caller's object straight through with no filtering, and through `Document.applyCellStyle` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:797-804). I grepped all in-repo call sites (`applyTableCellStyle`, `applyCellStyle`) and none currently pass explicit `undefined` for non-background keys, so this is a latent trap rather than a live break; MemDocStore (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:287) also does not mirror the deletion, it only merges the undefined value.

samples.summary: MemDocStore leaves the cleared key present-with-undefined while YorkieDocStore deletes it, so key-presence checks disagree between the two stores
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:287 does `cell.style = { ...cell.style, ...normalizeCellStyleClears(style) }`, leaving `backgroundColor: undefined` as an own property, whereas packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2445 `delete merged[key]` removes it entirely — the difference the PR's own new test asserts on (`expect('backgroundColor' in reread.style).toBe(false)`, packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2071). Every in-source consumer I checked reads the value truthily (packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:309, packages/docs/src/export/pdf-table-painter.ts:173, packages/docs/src/view/table-renderer.ts:175, packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3739), so nothing breaks today, but any `'backgroundColor' in cell.style` check — the exact idiom this PR's tests use — would evaluate differently depending on which store backs the document.

samples.summary: Cell-background Reset now emits a `removeStyleByPath` op whose undo support in the pinned Yorkie SDK I could not verify
samples.evidence: `undo()` is Yorkie-native (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2645-2650 `this.doc.history.undo()`), and this delta makes Reset produce a tree *style-removal* op (line 2461) where it previously produced only a merging `styleByPath`. If the pinned SDK (@yorkie-js/sdk 0.7.16, packages/frontend/package.json:93) does not generate a reverse operation for `removeStyleByPath`, Ctrl+Z after a cell-background Reset will not restore the color. The SDK is not vendored in this tree so I could not confirm; note the same pattern already exists for `applyCellSpan` (line 2513) and unlink (line 1902), so if broken it is a pre-existing class of bug this change extends to a new, easily-hit UI action.

finding.summary: Sibling "Reset" path for TABLE CELL background still passes `''` and is not normalized — the old color survives in the CRDT
finding.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-table-context-menu.tsx:230` calls `editor.applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: "" })` (the cell-background "Reset" button), which reaches `YorkieDocStore.applyCellStyle` (`yorkie-doc-store.ts:2410`). There the patch is merged verbatim (`const merged = { ...cell.style, ...style }`, line 2418), serialized by `serializeCellStyle` which SKIPS falsy values (`if (s.backgroundColor) attrs.backgroundColor = ...`, line 239), and written with `tree.styleByPath(...)` only (line 2430) — there is no `removeStyleByPath` counterpart as the inline path now has. Net effect: the local cache gets `cell.style.backgroundColor = ''` (cell looks cleared locally) while the Tree node keeps the previous `backgroundColor` attribute, so a peer or a reload still shows the old cell fill. This is the same empty-string-means-clear contract the diff establishes for inline styles (`normalizeStyleClears`), left unapplied on the sibling cell path that the very same picker UX drives. Fix belongs in `applyCellStyle` (normalize `''` → removal via `removeStyleByPath`) or by routing cell styles through an equivalent normalizer.

verdict.reason: The finding claims YorkieDocStore.applyCellStyle merges the style patch verbatim and writes only via tree.styleByPath with "no removeStyleByPath counterpart", leaving backgroundColor:'' dead in the CRDT. The code is not as described. At yorkie-doc-store.ts:2437 the patch is first passed through normalizeCellStyleClears (defined at packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:307-309 as the explicit table-cell counterpart of normalizeStyleClears, converting '' to undefined via CLEARABLE_CELL_COLOR_KEYS at types.ts:269). Line 2438 merges clearedStyle, not the raw style quoted in the finding. Lines 2443-2444 compute removedCellStyleAttrs(clearedStyle) (helper at lines 260-264, selecting present-but-undefined keys) and delete them from merged so the local cache stays consistent. Lines 2458-2462 then call tree.removeStyleByPath(cellPath, endPath, removeAttrs) - precisely the counterpart the finding says is absent. The cited line numbers (2410/2418/2430) fall on the adjacent editByPath method that ends at 2425, and the described code shape exists nowhere in the file, indicating the finding was written against a pre-fix revision. The asserted failure mode is additionally pinned by a negative test at packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2060-2074, which re-reads through a fresh YorkieDocStore (bypassing the optimistic cache) and asserts that 'backgroundColor' is absent from the re-read cell style while verticalAlign survives. Both call sites of applyTableCellStyle (docs-table-context-menu.tsx:233 and :246) route through editor.ts:3413-3434 into this same normalized path, so no bypassing sibling path exists.
